properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued August 4 at 10:19AM CDT until August 4 at 11:15AM CDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 1115 AM CDT.

* At 1019 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 23 nm southeast of Okaloosa Deep Water
Reef, or 31 nm southwest of Panama City Beach, moving east at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.area: Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 4 at 10:08AM CDT by NWS North Platte NE
properties.description:
At 1007 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
North Platte, moving east at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
North Platte, Maxwell, North Platte Airport, and Keith.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 97 between mile markers 1 and 11.
Interstate 80 in Nebraska between mile markers 173 and 186.
Highway 83 between mile markers 79 and 102.
properties.instruction:
Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 4 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA out 60 NM...
Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20
NM...

Radar and satellite imagery indicate a line of showers are capable of
generating funnel clouds or waterspouts until noon. Conditions will
become less favorable for waterspouts this afternoon as the sea
breeze begins to form along the beaches.
properties.area: Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20 NM; Coastal waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA out 20 NM; Waters from Edisto Beach SC to Savannah GA extending from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 4 at 10:54AM EDT until August 4 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Dare County in eastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Water over roadways. Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1052 AM EDT, North Carolina Department of Transportation
reported deep standing water along portions of NC 12 from Oregon
Inlet to the Waves, Salvo, and Rodanthe areas. Water has been
reported to be up to the headlights of some vehicles. Between 4
and 7 inches of rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Rodanthe, Waves, Salvo and Pea Island.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 8:54AM CDT until August 6 at 8:10PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 9.4 feet Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 34.1
feet on 10/08/2017.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued August 3 at 11:03AM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from good to moderate, but is forecasted to degrade.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM Wednesday, August 5, 2026.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
